I want you to solve GitHub issue #2903: implement the fix, validate it,
commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 3427b2ad84cc0d6ebacd963182cd4f1fed8f88c8
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

# Reporting

An ordinary end of turn is not completion. When finished, commit your solution
and send a message with FINAL REPORT on its own line within the first five lines,
followed by these six sections:
1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence.
2. Changes and reasons, including full base and final commit hashes.
3. Exact validation commands and results.
4. Before/after evidence on the issue's named repositories or witnesses.
5. git status --short, limitati

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The gap turned out not to be where the acceptance criterion pointed. The criterion asked for dynamic-index equality and disjointness, but exact-value index machinery already existed. Measuring ten Go shapes before writing code found the real blockers one layer down: the Go producer erased exact arithmetic at binding updates, and the flow layer never called its own widening operator. Reading the criterion alone would have led to reimplementing working code.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

FINAL REPORT

Issue #2903, bounded path and scalar reasoning for Go race candidates. Base commit `3427b2ad84cc0d6ebacd963182cd4f1fed8f88c8` (detached). Final commit `1fced533d02d65b726bee9fadce1ad1ca0919404`.

## 1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence

I measured ten paired Go shapes against the base commit before changing anything. The result was that **every index reaching the concurrency solver through a local integer variable stayed open**, even when its value was a compile-time constant:

| fixture | base behaviour |
|---|---|
| `i := 2; go indexWriter(values, i)` twice | `conflict siblings unordered open open loc=index reasons=["unknown_location"]` |
| `i := 0; j := 1` over one slice | same open row (a false positive kept open) |
| `i := 0; i += 3` vs literal `3` | open |
| two counted loops over disjoint halves | open |
| literal `2` in both children | already `proven exhaustive` |

The literal case already worked, so the defect is not the overlap gate. Three structured causes, each confirmed by dumping the IR or reading the call graph:

**Cause 1 — the index resolver stops at a memory load.** `canonicalize_bound_accesses` in `crates/bifrost-flow/src/concurrency.rs` resolved a dynamic index only through `invocation_scalar_integer`, which calls `direct_scalar_source` (`crates/bifrost-flow/src/typestate/production.rs:3190`). That walks `ValueFlowKind::Local | Parameter | Receiver | IntegerOffset` edges and returns `None` at any other producer and at any reassignment. A Go local read is none of those, so the chain never reached the literal.

**Cause 2 — a Go binding update erases exact arithmetic.** Dumping the semantics of `for index := 0; index < 2; index++` showed the increment lowering to `ValueFlow { kind: LanguageDefined, source: ValueId(11), target: ValueId(12) }` at point 27, immediately beside `GuardFact { predicate: OrderedIntegerComparison { LessThan, constant: ValueId(5) } }` at point 16. The ordered guard the earlier #2903 slice added had nothing to refine, because `increment_statement` (`crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/go/semantic.rs:8447`) published an opaque flow and ended the value's history at the update.

**Cause 3 — the scalar lattice has no finite height.** `ScalarIntegerInterval::widen` existed in `crates/bifrost-flow/src/scalar_state.rs:242` but was referenced only by its own unit test. The worklist joined with `hull` and relied on a `debug_assert` update bound. No production code constructs a finite `ScalarIntegerDomain::Signed` or `Unsigned`, so every interval is mathematical and a counting loop grew one value per iteration without converging. This had to be fixed before the derivation could run on arbitrary procedures.

A fourth observation explains why the existing closed-cell path did not help: `closed_scalar_cells` returned the empty set for every probe, because Go does not lower a plain local integer to a `LexicalCell`. A `:=` binding is an `Assignment` plus a `ValueFlow::Local`.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Base `3427b2ad84cc0d6ebacd963182cd4f1fed8f88c8` → final `1fced533d02d65b726bee9fadce1ad1ca0919404`, two commits:

- `c1e0d9df36ec93b3cfb6a11badf809f844df33a2` — the implementation and tests.
- `1fced533d02d65b726bee9fadce1ad1ca0919404` — the living ExecPlan update.

**`crates/bifrost-flow/src/scalar_state.rs`** — `ScalarFact::widen` lift
[... 10702 bytes omitted from the middle of this message ...]
 the work was connecting it rather than building it. Three things had to change. First, the flow layer never called its own widening operator, so the integer lattice had no finite height and a counting loop would have grown its interval one value per iteration; widening now applies once a program point has joined sixteen incoming states. Second, `x++`, `x--`, `x += n`, and `x -= n` published an opaque flow that ended the value's history at the update, which left every loop induction variable unknown and gave the ordered guard at the loop head nothing to refine; they now publish the same structured integer-offset relation the IR already carries for `x - 1`, which moves the Go adapter fingerprint to v76 without touching the IR schema. Third, the solver derives one scalar solution per invocation that owns an undecided element access, seeding each callee's formals from its caller's own derivation so a local passed as an argument crosses the call. An index that resolves to one element now names its location exactly as a literal index does, two element ranges that cannot meet reject the conflict, and an undecided index keeps its open result. Backing identity remains a separate proof, so equal index syntax over two slices stays separate and distinct syntax over one slice still races. Ten paired fixtures cover the decided element, disjoint elements, a stepped local, address mutation, an unknown index, disjoint and overlapping loop ranges, a loop past the widening limit, and both object near misses; five fail before the change and the five conservative controls pass on both sides. All twelve pinned revisions of the six-repository Go race corpus produce identical verdicts, identical scanned-file and byte census, and identical finding counts before and after. Still open on this issue: task-pairing exclusion beyond the existing sibling-spawn rule, exact WaitGroup and conditional protocol counts, a plain `name = <literal>` update, and finite Go integer widths, without which an interval cannot carry machine overflow semantics.
